OpenAI is redesigning the user interface of its ChatGPT mobile app for iOS and Android.
This version also includes a new navigation system with a bottom tab layout for easier access to multiple functions.
One intriguing new feature is a tab for background AI agents called “Dots,” which adds a new dimension to the application.
In addition, the updates also include an Explore centre and customisable pinned shortcuts for users, which significantly improve navigation and the overall user experience.
This major upgrade is intended to increase usability as the ecosystem of autonomous background agents and productivity tools continues to grow.
This upgrade is one of the biggest layout changes for the app so far.

The latest ChatGPT mobile UI upgrad e offers customers a more organised and simplified experience, with a multi-tab layout that is easily accessible from the bottom of the screen.

The Home Tab is still the main chat screen but now has the prompt “Ask anything” to make it more welcoming to users and currently has quick access to chat history via a slide-out menu for easier navigation.
There is a new Dedicated Dots tab next to the Home tab.
This tab helps AI agents better track and access active threads, improving the conversation management experience.
The Explore Hub also serves as a comprehensive directory of all the features available in ChatGPT.

It contains access to Codex, Images, Projects, Plugins, Space, Finance, Sites, Health integrations, and Scheduled tasks, all in one place, making it easier for users to engage with the wide range of options available in ChatGPT.

OpenAI has added the option to pin custom shortcuts to the app’s navigation bar, giving users a way to personalise their experience even more.
Users can long-press their favourite features like Projects, Codex, and Images on the Explore hub to pin them for quicker access.
This management is flexible, and users can change or remove shortcuts by clicking on “Unpin from the tab bar” when the tab bar reaches its capacity.
If you like the old look, you may go back to the original interface under Settings > New ChatGPT Design.
This means you may have an experience that’s customised for both new and returning users.
